questions.question_text:
Find $x$ around the point.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.9]\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\draw (O)--(0:2.3);\draw (O)--(85:2.3);\draw (O)--(218:2.3);\node at (0.55,0.7) {$85^{\circ}$};\node at (-0.75,0.15) {$133^{\circ}$};\node at (0.35,-0.8) {$x$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Adds the two known angles and reports their sum instead of the remaining sector.
Subtracts the two known angles from 265 rather than from a full 360-degree turn.
Subtracts only the difference between 133 and 85 from 360 degrees.

questions.question_text:
Four angles meet at one vertex.
Find $y$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.9]\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\draw (O)--(0:2.3);\draw (O)--(72:2.3);\draw (O)--(168:2.3);\draw (O)--(279:2.3);\node at (0.7,0.45) {$72^{\circ}$};\node at (-0.35,0.8) {$96^{\circ}$};\node at (-0.8,-0.35) {$111^{\circ}$};\node at (0.6,-0.65) {$y$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Subtracts the known total from 378 rather than from 360 degrees.
Reports the sum of the three known sectors instead of the missing sector.
Subtracts only 96 and 81 from 360 while ignoring the other known sectors.

questions.question_text:
The rays have been rotated together.
Find $b$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.9]\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\draw (O)--(25:2.3);\draw (O)--(129:2.3);\draw (O)--(246:2.3);\node at (0.3,0.8) {$104^{\circ}$};\node at (-0.8,0.05) {$117^{\circ}$};\node at (0.35,-0.75) {$b$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Adds the two known sectors and reports their total as the unknown.
Uses the difference between the two known angles and ignores the full turn.
Subtracts only the 41-degree difference from 360 degrees.

questions.question_text:
Three roads meet at a roundabout.
Two sectors are $144^{\circ}$ and $96^{\circ}$.
Find the third sector.

options.why: Adds the two given sectors and reports their total rather than the remainder.
Subtracts the known sectors from 300 instead of from a full turn.
Uses the difference between 144 and 96 instead of completing the revolution.

questions.question_text:
Five sectors at a point are $39^{\circ}$, $58^{\circ}$, $76^{\circ}$, $91^{\circ}$ and $x$.
Find $x$.

options.why: Adds all four known sectors and reports their total as the missing angle.
Subtracts only 39 plus 58 plus 76 from 360 and ignores 91 degrees.
Subtracts only 76 plus 66 plus 91 after miscopying the 58-degree sector.

questions.question_text:
Angles around a point include a right angle, $136^{\circ}$, $74^{\circ}$ and $q$.
Find $q$.

options.why: Subtracts only 136 plus 74 from 360 and ignores the right angle.
Adds all three known angles and reports their total instead of the remainder.
Subtracts the known total from 330 instead of from the full 360-degree turn.

questions.question_text:
3 angles meet at a point.
Tom and Katie are arguing about them!
Tom says the 3 angles cannot all be acute.
Katie says the 3 angles cannot all be obtuse.
Who is correct?

options.why: It overlooks that three acute angles cannot total 360 degrees.
Three obtuse angles can total 360 degrees, such as three 120-degree angles.
Tom is correct because three acute angles total less than 360 degrees.

questions.solution_text: Angles around a point total $360^\circ$. Three acute angles total less than $270^\circ$, so Tom is correct. Three obtuse angles can total $360^\circ$, for example $120^\circ+120^\circ+120^\circ$, so Katie is incorrect.
